controls.title: HSUP02

controls.title: HSUP03
controls.description: A breach of information by personnel is considered a security policy violation. Consequences of a security policy violation leads to a disciplinary process.

controls.title: HSUP04
controls.description: There are documented procedures for providing and revoking logical, and physical access when personnel join, have a role change or leave the organisation.

controls.title: HSUP05
controls.description: Asset management process(es) are in place.

controls.title: HSUP06
controls.description: Processes are in place for media equipment management, decommissioning and secure disposal.

controls.title: HSUP07
controls.description: An information security incident management process is in place.

controls.title: HSUP08
controls.description: Organisations have a documented, approved, business continuity and disaster recovery management, operational resilience policies and procedures in place.

controls.title: HSUP09
controls.description: Establish, document, approve, and implement rules to control physical and logical access to information and its assets.

controls.title: HSUP10
controls.description: The organisation's Board or information security steering committee is accountable for information security governance.

controls.title: HSUP11
controls.description: A documented policy and supporting procedures for maintaining physical security within the organisation is in place.

controls.title: HSUP12
controls.description: A documented and approved procedure to remove papers and removable storage from easily accessible areas is to be implemented.

controls.title: HSUP13
controls.description: Organisations have planned maintenance of information and services that are being provided to their customers via cloud services as per documented policies and agreements.

controls.title: HSUP14
controls.description: Information systems are securely designed, and appropriate controls are implemented.

controls.title: HSUP15
controls.description: A backup and recovery procedure is in place.

controls.description: A documented process is in place for performing changes to new and existing systems or services.

controls.title: HSUP17
controls.description: There is a documented and approved process for identifying vulnerabilities and updating patches on the organisation's systems, applications, tools, services etc.

controls.title: HSUP18
controls.description: Organisations, at a minimum, screen all personnel by verifying their identity, previous employment, applicable professional qualifications and criminal backgrounds before confirmation of employment.

controls.title: HSUP19
controls.description: Organisations are to ensure:  a)  information security responsibilities are clearly defined and assigned b)  a governance body or steering committee overseeing information security activities is in place c)  there is at least one individual responsible for maintaining information security within the organisation.

controls.title: HSUP20
controls.description: There has been an assessment of information security training needs and a training plan is put in place.

controls.title: HSUP21
controls.description: Organisations are to have roles and responsibilities determined to carry out the incident management process.

controls.title: HSUP22
controls.description: Establish criteria for developing business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience strategies, and capabilities based on disruption and impact to the organisation.

controls.title: HSUP23

controls.title: HSUP24
controls.description: Organisations are to integrate information security into project management.

controls.title: HSUP25
controls.description: Relevant legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements are identified and implemented.

controls.title: HSUP26
controls.description: A risk assessment methodology and cloud assurance activities that support the use of cloud technologies are in place.

controls.title: HSUP27
controls.description: Business, customer, and security requirements are identified, documented, and approved when developing or acquiring applications.

controls.title: HSUP28
controls.description: Risk assessments are performed on new, existing systems, and applications to understand the risks posed to the organisation while using them.

controls.title: HSUP29

controls.title: HSUP30

controls.title: HSUP33
controls.description: The complete lifecycle of the account(s) being used to access, process, or manage information and services is managed.

controls.title: HSUP34
controls.description: User accounts are authenticated and circumventing the authentication process is prevented.

controls.title: HSUP35
controls.description: Access to information and its associated assets is defined and authorised according to the business, customer and security requirements by adhering to the organisation's identity and access management policy or procedures.

controls.title: HSUP36
controls.description: Organisations are to ensure that only authorised users, software components and services are provided with privileged access rights.

controls.title: HSUP37
controls.description: Access to source code, development tools, and software libraries are restricted, appropriately managed, and maintained.

controls.title: HSUP38
controls.description: Metrics affecting the organisation's cyber security posture are regularly reported to the Board, and any decisions made are clearly documented.

controls.title: HSUP39
controls.description: Update, protect and maintain the devices installed as physical security safeguards including the utilities.

controls.title: HSUP40
controls.description: Secure areas of the organisation are protected from unauthorised personnel.

controls.description: Secure mechanisms are available and supported by a documented policy or guidelines to connect to the organisation's or customer's network.

controls.title: HSUP42

controls.title: HSUP43
controls.description: The organisation's architectural strategy supports the adoption of cloud technologies.

controls.title: HSUP44
controls.description: Organisations are to make use of developed and configured APIs for secure transfer of information between different cloud components.

controls.title: HSUP45
controls.description: Organisations are to ensure that appropriate controls are implemented to protect information in a multi-tenant cloud environment.

controls.title: HSUP46
controls.description: Networks and network devices that are used within the organisation are to be securely managed.

controls.title: HSUP47
controls.description: The systems and applications that are used to process, store, or transmit information are connected to a separate, dedicated network.

controls.title: HSUP48
controls.description: Backup copies of information, software, services provided, and relevant systems are protected and maintained in accordance with the backup and recovery procedures.

controls.title: HSUP49
controls.description: Backups are tested for their restoration in accordance with the documented backup and recovery procedures. Organisations are able to access restored backups as well.

controls.title: HSUP50
controls.description: Organisations developing inhouse systems, applications, or services are to maintain separate production and non-production environments.

controls.title: HSUP51
controls.description: Identified vulnerabilities or unpatched systems, services or applications are properly identified, tracked, and remediated.

controls.title: HSUP52
controls.description: Organisations have a standardised baseline configuration in place for new and existing systems, services, and applications.

controls.title: HSUP53
controls.description: The capacity requirements for maintenance of information processing facilities, communication, and environmental support during contingency operations are met.

controls.title: HSUP54
controls.description: Information, services, and applications on organisation systems and associated assets are protected against malware.

controls.title: HSUP55
controls.description: Organisations are to detect and prevent data leakage through the unauthorised disclosure and siphoning of information by individuals, systems, or services.

controls.title: HSUP56
controls.description: The lessons learned from business continuity and disaster recovery testing are reflected in the established and implemented information security controls.

controls.title: HSUP57
controls.description: Installed physical and environmental security mechanisms are monitored for potential security incidents.

controls.title: HSUP58
controls.description: Regular reviews are performed to confirm that the legal, regulatory, statutory, and contractual requirements are met.

controls.title: HSUP59
controls.description: Independent security reviews are defined and implemented before any new or major upgrades on systems are moved to the production environment.

controls.title: HSUP60
controls.description: Authorised personnel or teams are alerted upon unsuccessful backups.

controls.title: HSUP63
controls.description: Breach of employment and supplier agreements are enforced.

controls.description: Permissions for all personnel is restricted so that external media, unauthorised or malicious software is not installed on devices that are used to store, process or transfer health information.

controls.title: HMS10
controls.description: Up-to-date anti-virus, anti-malware/endpoint security software is installed on all computers and servers to protect health information and endpoint devices against malicious code or software.

controls.title: HMS11
controls.description: All relevant health information is backed up securely (as outlined in your documented policy) in an encrypted format and restoration is tested periodically.

controls.title: HMS12
controls.description: Only authorised devices that are managed and have security controls in place are to be used to process health information.

controls.title: HMS13
controls.description: When personnel are working remotely, security measures are in place to protect health information which could be accessed, processed, or stored outside the organisations premises.

controls.title: HMS14
controls.description: Licensed and secure software, tools or services are used to manage health information.

controls.title: HMS15
controls.description: Network services used for transmitting and receiving health information and data are kept secure, to ensure minimal security impact upon clinical practice.

controls.title: HMS16
controls.description: Devices processing or storing or transmitting health information are connected, where possible, to a separate network with heightened security away from other information and assets.

controls.title: HMS17
controls.description: Web traffic is encrypted for public facing websites which contain health information, so that they are protected against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks.

controls.title: HMS18
controls.description: All health information user activities are recorded, stored for a period of time and protected for analysis in case of a security incident.

controls.title: HMS19
controls.description: Unusual behaviour and potential information security incidents amongst endpoints and internal and external network traffic are detected.

controls.title: HMS20
controls.description: A documented and approved security incident management process is maintained, reviewed, and tested periodically.

controls.title: HMS21
controls.description: Availability of health information is to be maintained in the event of a service, system, or application being disrupted for a prolonged period.
